q: The total amount of radiation energy passing through per unit area and per unit time is called _____ and is measured in $W m^{-2}$.
e: The total amount of radiation energy passing through per unit area and per unit time is called irradiance and is measured in W m⁻². Solar energy is the Sun's radiant light and heat. Irradiance is that radiation per unit area per unit time. insolation or luminance is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Another commonly used term for irradiance of sunlight is _____.
e: Another commonly used term for irradiance of sunlight is insolation. Solar energy is the Sun's radiant light and heat. Irradiance is that radiation per unit area per unit time. illumination or radiation is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Above the earth's atmosphere, solar radiation has an intensity of approximately _____ $W m^{-2}$. This value is known as the solar constant.
e: Above the earth's atmosphere, solar radiation has an intensity of approximately 1350 W m⁻². This value is known as the solar constant. 1000 or 540 is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: At the earth's surface solar radiation has an intensity of approximately 1000 $W m^{-2}$ on a clear day at solar noon in the _____ months.
e: At the earth's surface solar radiation has an intensity of approximately 1000 W m⁻² on a clear day at solar noon in the summer months. winter or spring is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Earth's atmosphere and clouds absorb or scatter as much as _____ of the incoming sunlight.
e: Earth's atmosphere and clouds absorb or scatter as much as 54% of the incoming sunlight. 46% or 75% is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Conversion of light energy into electrical energy is based on a phenomenon called _____ effect.
e: Conversion of light energy into electrical energy is based on a phenomenon called photovoltaic effect. The photovoltaic effect turns light into electrical energy inside a semiconductor junction. photoelectric or thermoelectric is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: A solar cell is basically a _____ junction diode.
e: A solar cell is basically a p-n junction diode. A solar cell converts light to electricity; panels are modules made by combining cells. n-p or p-p is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Individual solar cells can be combined to form modules commonly known as solar _____.
e: Individual solar cells can be combined to form modules commonly known as solar panels. A solar cell converts light to electricity; panels are modules made by combining cells. arrays or grids is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Power conversion efficiency of the solar panel is the ratio of the electrical power delivered by the panel to the _____ power received by it.
e: Power conversion efficiency of the solar panel is the ratio of the electrical power delivered by the panel to the solar power received by it. A solar cell converts light to electricity; panels are modules made by combining cells. thermal or mechanical is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Flat plate collectors have copper pipes attached to an absorber plate contained in an insulated box that is covered with a tempered glass or _____ cover plate.
e: Flat plate collectors have copper pipes attached to an absorber plate contained in an insulated box that is covered with a tempered glass or polymer cover plate. metallic or ceramic is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Concentrated solar power (CSP) systems generate solar power by using mirrors or lenses to concentrate a large area of sunlight onto a specific point of receiver which converts into _____.
e: Concentrated solar power (CSP) systems generate solar power by using mirrors or lenses to concentrate a large area of sunlight onto a specific point of receiver which converts into heat. electricity or light is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: There are four types of CSP technologies: Parabolic trough systems, Linear fresnel systems, Power tower systems and _____ systems.
e: There are four types of CSP technologies: Parabolic trough systems, Linear fresnel systems, Power tower systems and Parabolic dish systems. Cylindrical or Spherical is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Wind energy is the _____ energy of air in motion.
e: Wind energy is the kinetic energy of air in motion. Wind power incident on area A is P = ½ρAv³, so it grows with the cube of wind speed. potential or thermal is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The output of a wind turbine is proportional to the dimensions of the rotor and to the _____ of the wind speed.
e: The output of a wind turbine is proportional to the dimensions of the rotor and to the cube of the wind speed. Wind power incident on area A is P = ½ρAv³, so it grows with the cube of wind speed. square or square root is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Theoretically, when wind speed doubles, wind power potential increases by a factor of _____.
e: Theoretically, when wind speed doubles, wind power potential increases by a factor of eight. Because P ∝ v³, doubling v multiplies power by 2³ = 8. four or two is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In a wind turbine, wind first hits the blades, causing them to rotate, changing kinetic energy to _____ energy.
e: In a wind turbine, wind first hits the blades, causing them to rotate, changing kinetic energy to rotational energy. electrical or thermal is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Wind turbines are mounted on a tower to capture the most energy. At 100 feet or more above ground, they can take advantage of the faster and less _____ wind.
e: Wind turbines are mounted on a tower to capture the most energy. At 100 feet or more above ground, they can take advantage of the faster and less turbulent wind. Turbulent flow is irregular and whirling, so speed and direction at a point keep changing. dense or humid is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: A windmill converts wind energy directly into _____ energy for such tasks as milling grain and pumping water.
e: A windmill converts wind energy directly into mechanical energy for such tasks as milling grain and pumping water. Wind power incident on area A is P = ½ρAv³, so it grows with the cube of wind speed. electrical or chemical is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The most common type of hydroelectric power plant is an _____ facility.
e: The most common type of hydroelectric power plant is an impoundment facility. Hydroelectric plants turn gravitational potential energy of water into kinetic energy and then electrical energy. diversion or pumped storage is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: A penstock is a closed conduit that channels the flow of water to turbines with water flow regulated by gates and _____.
e: A penstock is a closed conduit that channels the flow of water to turbines with water flow regulated by gates and valves. dams or spillways is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: A diversion, sometimes called a _____ facility, channels a portion of a river through a canal or a penstock.
e: A diversion, sometimes called a run-of-river facility, channels a portion of a river through a canal or a penstock. impoundment or pumped storage is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: When the demand for electricity is low, a PSH facility stores energy by pumping water from the lower reservoir to an _____ reservoir at a higher elevation.
e: When the demand for electricity is low, a PSH facility stores energy by pumping water from the lower reservoir to an upper reservoir at a higher elevation. intermediate or secondary is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The power available from falling water can be calculated from the flow rate and density of water, the height of fall, and the local acceleration due to _____.
e: The power available from falling water can be calculated from the flow rate and density of water, the height of fall, and the local acceleration due to gravity. friction or momentum is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In a hydroelectric plant, the difference in these two elevations (higher and lower) is known as the _____.
e: In a hydroelectric plant, the difference in these two elevations (higher and lower) is known as the head. Head is the elevation difference that sets the gravitational potential of the water. tail or drop is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The tidal energy is produced by the difference in sea levels due to the gravitational pull of mainly the _____ on the spinning earth.
e: The tidal energy is produced by the difference in sea levels due to the gravitational pull of mainly the moon on the spinning earth. sun or mars is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: A tidal barrage works similarly to a large hydropower reservoir dam but it is placed at the entrance to a bay or _____.
e: A tidal barrage works similarly to a large hydropower reservoir dam but it is placed at the entrance to a bay or estuary. delta or fjord is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Ocean thermal energy conversion plants can operate if the temperature difference between the water at the surface and water at depths up to 2 km is _____ K or more.
e: Ocean thermal energy conversion plants can operate if the temperature difference between the water at the surface and water at depths up to 2 km is 20 K or more. 10 or 30 is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The warm surface-water is used to boil a volatile liquid. The vapours of the liquid are then used to run the _____ of generator.
e: The warm surface-water is used to boil a volatile liquid. The vapours of the liquid are then used to run the turbine of generator. piston or rotor is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The kinetic energy of huge waves near the seashore can be trapped to generate electricity. The waves are generated by strong _____ blowing across the sea.
e: The kinetic energy of huge waves near the seashore can be trapped to generate electricity. The waves are generated by strong winds blowing across the sea. currents or tides is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Geothermal energy is a type of renewable energy taken from the Earth's core and it is one of the oldest types of natural sources of _____.
e: Geothermal energy is a type of renewable energy taken from the Earth's core and it is one of the oldest types of natural sources of heat. Geothermal energy is heat from the Earth's interior, used to drive turbines. light or electricity is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Thermal energy from _____ can be used to generate electricity. It is extremely hot liquid and semi-liquid rock located under Earth's surface.
e: Thermal energy from magma can be used to generate electricity. It is extremely hot liquid and semi-liquid rock located under Earth's surface. lava or crust is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Wells of up to a mile deep or more are drilled into underground _____ to tap into the geothermal resources.
e: Wells of up to a mile deep or more are drilled into underground reservoirs to tap into the geothermal resources. Geothermal energy is heat from the Earth's interior, used to drive turbines. aquifers or caves is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Biomass is renewable _____ material that comes from plants and animals.
e: Biomass is renewable organic material that comes from plants and animals. Biomass is renewable organic material from plants and animals. inorganic or synthetic is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Thermochemical conversion of biomass includes pyrolysis and _____.
e: Thermochemical conversion of biomass includes pyrolysis and gasification. Biomass is renewable organic material from plants and animals. fermentation or transesterification is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Biomass gasification produces a carbon monoxide and hydrogen rich gas called synthesis gas or _____.
e: Biomass gasification produces a carbon monoxide and hydrogen rich gas called synthesis gas or syngas. Biomass is renewable organic material from plants and animals. biogas or methane is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Chemical conversion process known as _____ is used for converting vegetable oils, animal fats, and greases into biodiesel.
e: Chemical conversion process known as transesterification is used for converting vegetable oils, animal fats, and greases into biodiesel. gasification or pyrolysis is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Biological conversion includes fermentation to convert biomass into ethanol and _____ digestion to produce natural gas.
e: Biological conversion includes fermentation to convert biomass into ethanol and anaerobic digestion to produce natural gas. Biomass is renewable organic material from plants and animals. aerobic or thermal is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Natural gas, also called biogas or biomethane, is produced in anaerobic digesters at sewage treatment plants and at dairy and _____ operations.
e: Natural gas, also called biogas or biomethane, is produced in anaerobic digesters at sewage treatment plants and at dairy and livestock operations. Coal, oil and natural gas are fossil fuels: non-renewable stores that form far slower than we burn them. agricultural or forestry is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Direct _____ is the most common method for converting biomass to useful energy.
e: Direct combustion is the most common method for converting biomass to useful energy. Biomass is renewable organic material from plants and animals. decomposition or fermentation is a different idea, so those options are wrong.
